footer.note: Fireemu is an independent open-source project, not an official Google or Firebase product.
landing.title: Fireemu — Test against Firebase as it behaves in production
landing.description: Fireemu is an unofficial local Firebase emulator for tests and CI, built to close the gap between local tests and production behavior.
landing.h1: Test against Firebase as it behaves in production
landing.lede: Fireemu is an unofficial local Firebase emulator, built to close the gap between local tests and production behavior.
landing.runTestsMeta: Starts Fireemu, runs your tests, then stops.
landing.productionHeading: Bring more of production into local tests.
landing.feature.index.title: Missing-index query rejection
landing.feature.index.body: Queries that need an undeclared composite index fail with FAILED_PRECONDITION under the default strict settings, so the missing index surfaces in the test run, before deployment.
landing.feature.totp.title: TOTP multi-factor authentication
landing.feature.totp.body: Test TOTP enrollment and sign-in through the Firebase SDK.
landing.feature.blocking.title: Blocking functions and account policies
landing.feature.blocking.body: Test blocking functions for sign-up, sign-in and password-reset emails. Verify account settings such as disabling user-initiated account deletion.
landing.feature.scheduled.title: Scheduled function execution
landing.feature.scheduled.body: Run Node.js scheduled functions by advancing the emulator clock. Test time zones and missed occurrences.
landing.feature.search.title: Enterprise full-text search
landing.feature.search.body: Run supported Firestore Enterprise text-search queries locally. Scores are approximate; Japanese/CJK tokenization has known differences.
landing.testingHeading1: Control time with a virtual clock.
landing.testingHeading2: Give each test its own Firebase environment.
landing.time.title: Test time-dependent behavior without waiting
landing.time.p1: Set and advance the emulator’s virtual clock to test token expiry and scheduled Node.js functions without waiting for real time to pass.
landing.time.p2: In the UI, choose a date and time, then run a scheduled function. You can also advance straight to its next scheduled run.
landing.worlds.title: Run integration tests in parallel
landing.worlds.p1: Each test world has its own data, Security Rules, Functions, ports and virtual clock—even with the same project ID. One test can change data or advance time without changing another world’s state.
landing.worlds.p2: withTestWorld starts the environment and cleans it up when the test finishes, including when it fails.
landing.worlds.boundary: Each script runs in its own world using the same demo-app project ID. Each callback advances only its world’s clock.
landing.verification.intro: Fireemu’s responses are compared with recordings from real Firebase projects. The published records describe the conditions checked, reviewed differences, and work still in progress.
landing.step.record.title: Record
landing.step.record.body: Observe responses from real Firebase projects.
landing.step.compare.title: Compare
landing.step.compare.body: Check local behavior against those recordings.
landing.step.publish.title: Publish the scope
landing.step.publish.body: Keep verified conditions and known differences inspectable.
landing.verification.boundary: Verification applies to the recorded scope, not every Firebase feature or input. Before relying on results in CI, compare critical workflows with a dedicated Firebase test project—not your live production project.
landing.differs.title: Where local behavior differs.
landing.differs.p1: Some production setup is relaxed for local tests. Features such as MFA and multi-tenancy are enabled by default; documented settings let you test their production setup requirements.
landing.differs.p2: Other behavior remains approximate or outside the local runtime, including text analysis, real quota accounting and cloud infrastructure. We distinguish these limits from behavior that is not yet implemented or verified.
landing.services.intro: Find the services your app uses. Each guide describes the supported APIs and their limits.
landing.service.firestore.name: Cloud Firestore
landing.service.firestore.covers: Standard and Enterprise editions, index validation, queries and Security Rules.
landing.service.firestore.limit: Enterprise pipelines and text search have a documented scope.
landing.service.auth.name: Firebase Authentication
landing.service.auth.covers: Identity Platform settings, sign-in, TOTP/SMS MFA, tenants and blocking functions.
landing.service.auth.limit: Live flows to external identity providers are outside the local runtime.
landing.service.storage.name: Cloud Storage
landing.service.storage.covers: Firebase and JSON APIs, object operations and Security Rules.
landing.service.storage.limit: Managed infrastructure and API coverage have limits; see the guide.
landing.service.functions.name: Cloud Functions
landing.service.functions.covers: Node.js and Python functions: HTTP, callable, event, blocking, scheduled and task-queue functions (Cloud Tasks).
landing.service.pubsub.name: Cloud Pub/Sub
landing.service.pubsub.covers: Topics, subscriptions, push/pull delivery, dead-letter topics and StreamingPull.
landing.service.pubsub.limit: Schemas, BigQuery/Storage delivery and exactly-once delivery are not supported.
landing.service.eventarc.name: Eventarc
landing.service.eventarc.covers: Custom events, channels and event delivery to local Functions.
landing.service.eventarc.limit: See the supported event types and authentication settings in the guide.
landing.service.rtdb.name: Realtime Database
landing.service.rtdb.covers: REST and realtime protocols, Security Rules, export and import.
landing.service.rtdb.limit: Production verification covers recorded cases; no official-emulator parity claim.
landing.service.hosting.name: Firebase Hosting
landing.service.hosting.covers: Static files, redirects, rewrites, headers, clean URLs and localization.
landing.service.hosting.limit: Production verification covers recorded cases; no official-emulator parity claim.
landing.service.appcheck.name: Firebase App Check
landing.service.appcheck.covers: Debug-token exchange and local application flows using App Check tokens.
landing.service.appcheck.limit: Real-device attestation and limited-use replay protection are not supported.
landing.services.notSupported: Not currently supported: App Hosting and Data Connect.
landing.workflowHeading: From local setup to your test suite.
landing.workflow.install.title: Install
landing.workflow.install.body: Add the fireemu package to your project and create fireemu.toml with init.
landing.workflow.connect.title: Connect
landing.workflow.connect.body: Point the Firebase SDKs at the local services. Under exec, the Admin SDK needs no code.
landing.workflow.run.title: Run tests
landing.workflow.run.body: Wrap your test command in exec. Fireemu starts, runs the command, and exits with its status.
landing.workflow.ci.title: Use in CI
landing.workflow.ci.body: Run the same command in CI. Review the isolation and environment settings first.
landing.migrate: Already using the Local Emulator Suite? Fireemu reads your existing firebase.json as it is.
